question: The Commission announced that the first eight national plans under the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) Regulation1 have been approved and that it has submitted proposals for financial assistance to the Council for Belgium, Bulgaria, Denmark, Spain, Croatia, Cyprus, Portugal and Romania. 19 Member States have submitted national defence investment plans under SAFE.

Under Article 1 of the SAFE Regulation, financial assistance may support procurement for two categories of defence products. Article 2 defines common procurement as conducted by one Member State together with at least one other Member State, an EEA EFTA state or with Ukraine. Article 4(3) allows procurement by a single Member State to be financed under SAFE until 30 May 2026. 1.
How many of the 19 national plans’ proposed activities address each type of product listed in categories one and two?
How many of the submitted national defence investment plans include procurement activities involving Ukraine, and what is the total share of SAFE funding allocated to activities involving Ukraine?

How many Member States have submitted procurement activities carried out by only one Member State pursuant to Article 4(3) and what share of the requested SAFE funding is allocated to single-state procurement, also how many of the activities submitted by the 19 Member States involve procurement by two participating states, compared with three or more states?
OJ L, 2025/1106, 28.5.2025, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/1106/oj.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.3.2026) By the regulatory deadline of 30 November 2025, 19 Member States submitted their national defence investment plans under the Security Action for Europe Regulation (SAFE)1. These plans collectively account for nearly two years of defence equipment procurement for the EU272, demonstrating a commitment to scaling up European defence readiness.

Regarding the product categories, the submitted plans are comprehensive and cover all capability categories set out in Article 1 of the SAFE Regulation, which reflect the priority areas identified by the European Council.

While the detailed breakdown of each activity remains sensitive due to the nature of the national defence data involved, the Commission can confirm that the requested funding involves both Category 1 and Category 2 products. In line with the EU's commitment to Ukraine's security, support to Ukraine is a core feature of SAFE.

The vast majority of the submitted national plans include procurement activities involving in different manners Ukraine. On procurement structures, SAFE incentivizes cooperation. To date, there is a pre-dominance of cooperative procurement, which represents more than 65% of the total planned activities, amounting to approximately EUR 98 billion.

It is worth mentioning that current single procurement projects include provisions to extend the benefit of the contract to additional SAFE eligible partners. The Commission is currently finalizing its assessment of the remaining plans.

A comprehensive report, which will provide additional detailed information on the implementation of SAFE and the specific breakdown of activities, is scheduled to be presented to the European Parliament in May 2026.
